A bright arcing strand runs from bracer to scute and the glowing capillary field meets the root. Fine secondary filaments are also visible, so the incidental single-cord count is not exact.
Opposed upper and lower rim grips and direct scute/root contact remain readable together.

Water still pours visibly from the root into a large fresh splash. A single image supports a present leak but does not establish that flow has diminished from its prior state; the intended narrowing is unproved.
The open bracer rim and connected scute suggest donation, but the picture does not clearly establish a missing armour plate or how much protection she gave up.
The seedlings are clearly above the flooded trough behind the repair, connecting life to the site. Their imminent danger, a rising tide and a successful rescue are not visually established.

The rendered opening is larger and its upper arch reaches out of frame, unlike the planned complete small doorway. The local lining-to-fold relation is still visible for the source-specific M08 tests.
